checkedAlternates.risk: Card numbers are typed into websites constantly, so a credit card can read as an online payment.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The third row is the physical card presented at a counter; the fourth row has no card to hand over at all.

checkedAlternates.risk: A mobile wallet stores a card, and the phone is tapped at the same terminal.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Nothing but the phone changes hands, and the phone is the device the whole fourth row runs on.

checkedAlternates.risk: A gift card carries a fixed stored value and spends like cash.
checkedAlternates.resolution: It is still a card you hand to the cashier, which is what the row is sorted by.

checkedAlternates.risk: Barter is money-adjacent enough that a player may read coins as an early form of it.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Barter is the only method on the board with no money in it at all, which is why it is the single-item row.

authorReview.notes: The rule is what physically leaves your hand. That is why the mobile wallet is not a card, even though it holds one.

blindPlaytest.notes: The card row and the phone row are the same idea a decade apart. If testers merge them, relabel the third row as "A plastic card you hand to the cashier".
